title: Quick check: Controlled Components

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Controlled Components”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
State-controlled input values should provide labels, validation feedback, and a recoverable input experience.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: State-controlled input values should provide labels, validation feedback, and a recoverable input experience.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Controlled Components: State-controlled input values should provide labels, validation feedback, and a recoverable input experience.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying State-controlled input values?
options: Keep useful values on validation failure and associate each input with a label and error message.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Keep useful values on validation failure and associate each input with a label and error message.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Controlled Components: Keep useful values on validation failure and associate each input with a label and error message.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Controlled Components” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Controlled Components: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
